status: draft — 100 cases proposed, none reviewed yet. The set is complete in size and coverage and is waiting on human review; see README.md.
description: Reviewed golden set for the helpdesk agent: one ticket per case, with the classification, runbook, outcome, answer content and protected text a person has decided are right. Only cases with review.status "reviewed" are ground truth. The labelling guidelines the expectations follow are README.md, at label_version v1.

docs.title: Setting up MFA on a new phone

notes: VIP requesters always go to a person (vip_always_human).
No tool is whitelisted for unattended use, so no case expects the `action` outcome.
A runbook counts as support at a similarity of 0.62 or more (kb_support_floor).
Secrets are scrubbed from the stored body at intake (scrub_secrets_at_rest).
P1 routes to oncall; everything else to tier1.

changes: 46 draft cases added, taking the set to the 100 the P2 gate asks for: every category has at least 9, and each safety flag now has cases on both sides of its line.

The labelling guidelines the expectations follow are written down for the first time, as README.md, at label_version v1 — G1 to G14, with the rules the earlier rationales cited by number but never defined.

Gaps the earlier 54 left, now covered: the clarify_exhausted rule and the injection rule had no case that reached them; link_incident had one case; every scope exclusion in the runbooks (warehouse scanners, warehouse tablets, mobile VPN) is now the near miss in a case that must not follow it.
Still nothing is reviewed. A draft is a proposal whatever wrote it, and the set becomes ground truth one accepted case at a time.

54 draft cases across all eight categories and every scenario: straightforward, technical, ambiguous, multi-turn, internal note, attachment, AI draft edited before sending, sensitive information, backfilled (legacy) tickets, security, destructive, prompt injection, known incident and VIP.
Expectations drafted by an AI assistant from the runbooks, the triage prompt's priority definitions and decide.ts, without looking at system output. None is ground truth until a person reviews it.
